title: Season End, Carry-Over and Closure of a Mountain Dining Plans Record
content:
A plan in the Mountain Dining Plans range runs to the end of the season it was sold for and then stops being spendable. Where the plan allows carry-over, the balance up to the plan's carry-over ceiling moves to the plan the household opens for the next season, and anything above the ceiling must be used before the season ends or is lost. Where the plan does not allow carry-over, the balance left must be used within the plan's post-season period and is otherwise lost; bonus money never carries over whatever the plan says about the rest. A plan record is closed only when no plan fee is left to collect and no balance is left to spend or return. Closing is the last entry on the record and nothing is added to it afterwards, so a transaction that reaches the collective late is settled against the outlet rather than against the closed plan.

## What becomes of a balance at the end of the season

| The plan | Loaded money left on it | Bonus money left on it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| allows carry-over | up to the plan's carry-over ceiling moves to the plan the household opens for the next season; anything above the ceiling is to be used before the season ends, and is otherwise lost | does not carry over |
| does not allow carry-over | to be used within the plan's post-season period, and is otherwise lost | does not carry over |

The exclusion of bonus money holds on both rows: bonus never carries over, whatever the plan provides about the rest of the balance.

**A carry-over reading on hypothetical figures.** A plan allows carry-over with a ceiling of $500.00 and ends the season with $640.00 standing on it. Of that, $500.00 is what the ceiling admits and moves to the plan opened for the next season; the remaining $140.00 stands above the ceiling and is to be used before the season ends, failing which it is lost.

## When a record is closed

Closure is reached on two conditions together, both read from the collective's own record of the plan and both read before the record is closed:

1. no plan fee is left to collect on the plan, and
2. no balance is left on it to spend or to return.

Where either still stands, the record is not closed. Closing is the last entry made on the record, and nothing is added to it afterwards; a transaction that reaches the collective after the record was closed is therefore settled against the outlet it arose at rather than against the plan.
